data_center.body: Available records list 1,556 data-center sites in development, equal to 0.51 times the 3,068 operating sites; 894 sites are in the tracked active pipeline. Recent reports show individual large projects moving forward: Fluidstack began construction on a 99-acre campus in Virginia, and Fluor won the engineering, procurement and construction contract for a $4 billion Kentucky campus. These projects show activity reaching the construction and contracting stages, but they do not measure the conversion rate of the national pipeline.
data_center.headline: Campus projects move into contracting and construction while 1,556 sites remain in development

economic_impact.body: Aggregate outcomes shifted to a less favorable mix. Nonfarm-business productivity growth eased slightly to 2.1% and real output growth to 2.3%, while unit labor cost growth rose materially to 2.4%. The labor-share index remains 8.3% below 2020, despite a slight improvement in the latest reading. These economy-wide measures do not isolate AI’s contribution, but they show a moderation in measured productivity growth alongside stronger labor-cost growth.
economic_impact.headline: Productivity eases as unit labor cost growth rises

grid_storage.body: Electric-power construction growth accelerated materially to 14.0%. At the same time, the active interconnection queue totals 2,061 GW, including 552.7 GW of storage, and only 24.2% of queued capacity has reached executed-agreement or construction stages. Current infrastructure work is expanding quickly, but most proposed generation and storage capacity remains at earlier stages of development.
grid_storage.headline: Power construction accelerates, but most queued capacity remains at earlier stages

macro.body: Market support for AI-linked activity has weakened. The share of covered companies with positive one-year returns fell materially to 60.8%, and the median return declined to 10.0%. The AI Equity Index and average sector trading pressure also edged lower. Most covered companies remain positive over one year, but the retreat across all four measures marks a reversal of the previous broadening in performance. The physical expansion remains substantial. Available records show 1,556 data-center sites in development, roughly half the 3,068 operating sites, with 894 sites in the tracked active pipeline. The finance measures do not yet show a current cash-flow shortfall: operating cash flow equals 1.23 times CapEx. Reserves, however, cover only 0.85 years of spending, and borrower strain of 30.2 remains above lender strain of 19.6. Reuters also reported that Nvidia’s AI-financing activity may continue with less risk appetite, adding a concrete sign that some financing could become more selective. Business deployment remains partial. Current AI use is reported by 24.6% of businesses, compared with 28.6% expecting use within six months, a gap of four percentage points. Separately, 60.8% of adults ages 18–64 report some generative-AI use, though that measure is not directly comparable with organization-level adoption. A recent survey also reported that businesses are moving to build AI-agent workforces while traditional management practices lag. Large physical commitments are therefore meeting cooler market signals before business use and supporting organizational practices have become broad.
macro.headline: The AI buildout remains large as market support cools and business use stays partial

market.body: The equity signal has softened across the covered universe. Companies with positive one-year returns fell materially to 60.8%, and the median return declined materially to 10.0%. The AI Equity Index slipped to 36.6 and average sector trading pressure to 43.2. Most covered companies remain positive over one year, but the simultaneous decline in breadth and typical performance indicates that the previous improvement has partly unwound.
market.headline: Equity breadth and typical returns retreat

power.body: Commercial electricity demand is growing 3.5%, nearly twice the 1.8% increase in total retail demand, while retail electricity prices are up 5.1%. Reuters reported that SpaceX plans a $24 billion gas-power and data-center project in Texas. The proposal is a notable example of generation being planned alongside data-center capacity, but it remains a reported plan and cannot explain the national demand figures. Across the broader pipeline horizon, net planned generation additions total 227.6 GW.
power.headline: A reported $24 billion SpaceX plan combines a data center with gas generation

editorial_briefing.style_reference: AI Macro is a research platform that examines the development of the U.S. AI economy from capital investment and physical construction through deployment, adoption, and economic results. It uses publicly available data to relate corporate and market activity to the physical systems required to support the buildout. It evaluates the extent to which that investment produces durable economic value and how its effects are transmitted through the broader U.S. economy.

body.text: The market signal improved in breadth but weakened in intensity. The share of covered companies with positive one-year returns rose materially to 63.2%, and the median return edged up to 10.8%. At the same time, the AI Equity Index slipped to 35.8 and average sector trading pressure fell materially to 40.9. CoreWeave reported revenue above expectations and raised guidance, easing reported concerns about an AI slowdown. The broader readings nevertheless point to wider participation rather than uniformly stronger market conditions.

headline.text: Equity breadth improves as trading pressure falls

body.text: The active interconnection queue totals 2,061 GW, including 552.7 GW of storage, but only 24.2% has reached executed-agreement or construction stages. Historical conversion provides a harder benchmark: just 13% of the 2000–2020 queue cohort reached operation. Grid operators have filed large-load interconnection reforms at FERC, placing process changes on the regulatory agenda. Those filings address how major new users connect, but they do not alter the current gap between queued and operating capacity.

headline.text: Most of the 2,061 GW interconnection queue remains at earlier stages

body.text: Nonfarm-business productivity grew 2.1% and real output 2.3%, but real hourly compensation increased only 0.6%. Unit labor costs rose 2.4%. The result is positive growth in output per hour without a comparable gain in workers’ real hourly pay. These aggregate measures do not isolate AI’s contribution, but they provide little evidence that current productivity growth is already translating into broad compensation gains.

headline.text: Productivity growth continues to outpace real hourly compensation
Equity breadth improves while the power pipeline remains difficult to convert

paragraphs.text: Equity performance has broadened even as the aggregate market signal has softened. The share of covered companies with positive one-year returns rose materially to 63.2%, and the median return reached 10.8%. Yet the AI Equity Index slipped to 35.8 and average sector trading pressure fell materially to 40.9. CoreWeave’s revenue beat and higher guidance eased reported slowdown concerns, but the wider data show improved breadth rather than a uniformly stronger AI trade.

Physical expansion remains large, but converting plans into usable capacity is uncertain. Available records show 1,556 data-center sites in development, about half the 3,068 operating sites. Commercial electricity demand is growing 3.5%, faster than the 1.8% increase in total retail demand. Against that demand, the active interconnection queue totals 2,061 GW, yet only 24.2% is in executed-agreement or construction stages, and just 13% of the 2000–2020 queue cohort reached operation. Grid operators have filed large-load interconnection reforms at FERC, but the queue remains a measure of proposals and progress rather than delivered supply.

Aggregate economic results remain positive but do not identify an AI payoff. Nonfarm-business productivity grew 2.1% and real output 2.3%, while real hourly compensation rose 0.6% and unit labor costs increased 2.4%. Current AI use is reported by 24.6% of businesses, so deployment remains partial. These measures cannot isolate AI’s contribution, and compensation growth remains well below the measured gains in productivity and output.

You are writing the current research update for AI Macro.

Use only the findings and recent developments in the supplied briefing. Decide what matters, connect related evidence when the relationship is supported, and explain it in clear, natural English for an intelligent general reader. Prioritize significance over coverage. It is fine for the evidence to be mixed. Do not force unrelated facts into one story.

The style reference shows the desired level of restraint, specificity, and sentence construction. Match those qualities without copying its wording. Write like a careful human analyst. Use concrete subjects and verbs. Avoid rhetorical gimmicks and artificial-sounding transitions. Do not mention the prompt, the briefing, evidence IDs, validation, methodology, or the writing process.

On a normal update, candidate_domains identifies sections that may deserve replacement. Update only the domain Reads for which you can write something materially more useful than the prior publication; you may return no domain Reads when none deserves replacement. On a bootstrap publication, write every candidate domain because no prior Read exists. Always write one new Macro Read that explains the most important current story across the platform in two to four coherent paragraphs.

Do not inventory every supplied metric or news item. Use a number only when it helps the reader understand magnitude. Use recent developments when they materially sharpen the interpretation of the measured findings. Treat news reports as reported developments, not as proof of a broader causal claim.

Attach only the fact_ids and event_ids that actually support each passage. Those IDs are citations for the application and must never appear in the prose. Do not invent numbers, facts, events, causes, or forecasts.

Return only the structured response.

adoption.analysis: Current AI use is reported by 24.6% of businesses, compared with 28.6% expecting use within six months, a 4.0-percentage-point gap between deployment and intent. Reported use is much higher among adults: 60.8% of those ages 18–64 use some generative AI, although that consumer measure is not directly comparable with organization-level use of AI more generally. A newly reported enterprise study found adoption outpacing AI assurance, identifying assurance as a separate implementation issue rather than simply another measure of adoption.

compute.analysis: Semiconductor and electronic-component output grew 19.9%, roughly three times the 6.5% rate for computer and peripheral equipment. Yet semiconductor capacity utilization was 76.5%, below the 81.3% rate for computer equipment. The industry aggregates therefore show much stronger semiconductor production growth without higher overall utilization. Reuters separately reported that Chinese AI firms were rushing to secure Nvidia chip capacity amid concern about U.S. curbs, showing why access to specific advanced chips may differ from broad manufacturing conditions.

macro.analysis: Equity performance has broadened even as the aggregate market signal has softened. The share of covered companies with positive one-year returns rose materially to 63.2%, and the median return reached 10.8%. Yet the AI Equity Index slipped to 35.8 and average sector trading pressure fell materially to 40.9. CoreWeave’s revenue beat and higher guidance eased reported slowdown concerns, but the wider data show improved breadth rather than a uniformly stronger AI trade. Physical expansion remains large, but converting plans into usable capacity is uncertain. Available records show 1,556 data-center sites in development, about half the 3,068 operating sites. Commercial electricity demand is growing 3.5%, faster than the 1.8% increase in total retail demand. Against that demand, the active interconnection queue totals 2,061 GW, yet only 24.2% is in executed-agreement or construction stages, and just 13% of the 2000–2020 queue cohort reached operation. Grid operators have filed large-load interconnection reforms at FERC, but the queue remains a measure of proposals and progress rather than delivered supply. Aggregate economic results remain positive but do not identify an AI payoff. Nonfarm-business productivity grew 2.1% and real output 2.3%, while real hourly compensation rose 0.6% and unit labor costs increased 2.4%. Current AI use is reported by 24.6% of businesses, so deployment remains partial. These measures cannot isolate AI’s contribution, and compensation growth remains well below the measured gains in productivity and output.

water.analysis: The broad county-level drought screen improved materially: 261 campuses, or 17.5% of those with county data, are in counties containing some D2-or-worse drought area. The more concentrated screen moved in the opposite direction. The count in counties where at least one-quarter of the area is D2 or worse rose slightly to 193 campuses, or 13.0%. Attach only the fact_ids and event_ids that actually support each passage. Those IDs are citations for the application and must never appear in the prose. Do not invent numbers, facts, events, causes, or forecasts.

Return only the structured response.
